text:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected: multiple model artifact fetch failures from Hugging Face registry for model redwood/large-v2 while scaling up hosts. Error rate crossing threshold. Auto-ticket opened.
anya: seeing spikes in cold-start errors, users hitting 500s on generation requests. Investigating artifact pull logs now.
infra-swe: logs show HF registry returning 429 for several artifact GETs. Also some 502s from the signed-url CDN. sample:
```
GET https://hf.co/api/models/redwood/large-v2/resolve -> 429 Too Many Requests
curl -i 'https://huggingface.co/redwood/large-v2/resolve/main/pytorch_model.bin'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-reset: 202
```
sophia: confirmed — our prefetch workers are retrying aggressively which is worsening bursts. we have exponential backoff but the retry concurrency is high during deploys.
michael: how bad is customer impact? any production customers 1:1s affected?
customer-success: we've already got 2 customers reporting model errors and one internal smoke test failing. potential degradation for all hosted customers using that model until fetches succeed or we fallback.
infra-swe: timeline: deploy started at 1972103300, prefetch jobs started 1972103310, error surge at 1972103450. Prefetch concurrency ~120, HF rate limit for our org appears to be ~100/10s (approx).
engops: possible immediate mitigations: 1) throttle prefetch concurrency globally 2) switch serving to fall back to cached quantized variant (redwood/large-v2-q4) 3) enable S3 mirror if prefetched artifacts exist
anya: agree. start with throttling prefetches and enable fallback route. doing ramp-down now.
```
# throttle prefetch workers
kubectl scale deploy prefetch-workers --replicas=4 -n infra
# mark model fallback in config
redwoodctl rollout set-fallback redwood/large-v2 -> redwood/large-v2-q4
```
infra-swe: throttle applied. reduced prefetch replicas from 12 -> 4. observing less outbound to HF, 429s rate dropping.
observability-bot: Metric spike: artifact_fetch_429 from 0.02 -> 0.47 across region-us-west in 5m. ErrorBudget alert firing.
kim: started canary flip to q4 fallback for route /models/redwood/large-v2 on dedicated and hosted canaries.
michael: I'm taking on-call. anya, please hand over current state and actions done. I'll coordinate escalations and comms.
anya: handoff: root cause appears to be HF registry rate-limiting our artifact resolve requests during deploy prefetch. Actions so far: scaled down prefetch workers, activated fallback to q4 variant on canary, notified CS. Next steps: setup temporary mirror if artifacts available in our S3 cache and contact HF support.
michael: got it. priority: 1) prevent further cold-start failures for live traffic (fallback already in progress), 2) reduce upstream pressure (prefetch throttled), 3) bring up S3 mirror and validate integrity, 4) engage HF support and request rate-limit raise or guidance.
engops: I'll run S3 mirror publish for available artifacts. publishing from artifact-cache bucket -> s3://redwood-hf-mirror/redwood/large-v2/
```
aws s3 cp s3://artifact-cache/redwood/large-v2/ s3://redwood-hf-mirror/redwood/large-v2/ --recursive
# then update artifact_mirror config
redwoodctl config set artifact_mirror_url https://mirror.redwood.example.com/hf
```
sophia: note: we need to ensure the mirror is used only when upstream returns 429/5xx; don't bypass HF permanently.
infra-swe: deploying mirror proxy and updating resolver policy now. adding circuit-breaker: if 429s > 1% over 2m then route to mirror.
observability-bot: mirror proxy health checks passing. artifact_fetch_429 decreased to 0.12 in last 3m. cold-start error rate decreased by ~70% on canary.
customer-success: sending proactive note to impacted customers: short blurb drafted for review. will wait for michael signoff.
michael: approved. CS, send note with current mitigations and ETA to full recovery: 60-90m. escalate to HF support channel and include logs & rate-limit headers.
anya: pinging HF support: attaching sample headers and deploy pattern. HF support case #INC-8421 created.
engops: mirror publish completed. validating checksum against original: all checksums match.
```
# checksum verify
sha256sum s3://redwood-hf-mirror/redwood/large-v2/pytorch_model.bin
```
kim: rolling out fallback to remaining production hosts. will keep 10% traffic on upstream to monitor.
sophia: we should also temporarily reduce prefetch concurrency permanently for this model to avoid repeated bursts during deploys. propose default 16.
michael: agreed. set prefetch concurrency limit for redwood/large-v2 to 16 and codify in model config.
infra-swe: change applied. prefetch concurrency now 16. also added backoff multiplier to retries (2x -> 4x) and jitter.
observability-bot: artifact_fetch_429 now 0.03, cold-start errors close to baseline. No new customer complaints in last 15m.
michael: final notes for on-call handoff later: root cause appears to be upstream HF rate-limits triggered by our high concurrent prefetch during a deploy. mitigations: throttled prefetch, enabled q4 fallback, published mirror, updated resolver to circuit-breaker, adjusted retries.
michael: next actions for follow-up (owner tags): engops - monitor mirror + cost impact; infra-swe - codify prefetch concurrency and backoff policy; devex - consider distributed prefetch stagger for large model rollouts; customer-success - follow-up messages to impacted customers with RCA when available.
anya: thanks everyone. handing back to support-rotation at 1972106556. please ping if HF responds with different guidance.
michael: handing off to night on-call @oncall-1. tagging page for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
oncall-1: acknowledged, will monitor overnight and start postmortem draft if needed.
